articles.title: ChatGPT Chrome Extension Expands Browser Access to Read Open Tab Content
articles.summary:
OpenAI has announced an expanded Chrome integration that lets ChatGPT gather information from open browser tabs and take action within the browser. This update introduces two distinct workflows: “Chat,” which uses tab content to inform its responses, and “Work,” which can control tabs to complete tasks. articles.title: Hackers Exploit Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS Flaw to Bypass MFA and Deploy Ransomware
articles.summary:
Ransomware operators are exploiting a vulnerability in Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS that allows them to bypass authentication. This issue enables unauthorized VPN sessions, bypasses multifactor authentication (MFA), and allows access to corporate networks. According to Unit 42’s October 19 update, two groups, Spikey Scorpius (also referred to as Qilin) and Tarnished Scorpius, are using CVE-2026-0257. […]

articles.title: Hackers Compromise OVHcloud GitHub Repository to Distribute Secret-Stealing Malware
articles.summary:

articles.title: Hackers Can Take Over WordPress Websites Without a Password Using Two Security Flaws
articles.summary:
Hackers can compromise vulnerable WordPress websites without stealing passwords by chaining two security flaws in the platform’s core. Disclosed in July 2026, the chain involves CVE-2026-63030 and CVE-2026-60137. Unlike attacks dependent on vulnerable extensions, WP2Shell affects default WordPress installations without requiring a third-party plugin. articles.title: Hackers Exploit Zimbra Zero-Click Flaw to Take Control of Email Servers
articles.summary:
Hackers are exploiting a command injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-73570) in the Zimbra Collaboration Suite. This vulnerability allows attackers to compromise internet-facing email servers without any user interaction. Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed attackers deploying webshells, escalating privileges, collecting authentication secrets, and staging mailbox data across organizations in various regions and industries. articles.title: Hackers Turn Low-Cost Android Phones Into Hidden Proxy Botnets Through Preinstalled Malware
articles.summary:
